anomalies.observed: Both fan-tach signal paths have series diodes oriented with their cathodes toward the fan headers and anodes toward the MCU-side pull-ups and inputs: D5.3 is on NET0005 with J9.3, while D5.1 is on Net-(D5-A) with R1 and GPIO21; D9.3 is on NET0001 with J1.3, while D9.1 is on Net-(D9-A) with R5 and GPIO20. The MCU-side pull-ups are 10 kΩ to +3V3.
anomalies.expected: The tach inputs should pass fan tach pulses to the MCU. For the usual open-collector fan tach output, the low-going pulses must be able to pull the MCU input low; the series diode orientation should not block that path.

evidence.quote: Monitors 2 fan tachometers (NUM_FANS = 2) with TVS-diode-protected inputs, and raises a run fault if a fan stalls.

anomalies.impact: With typical open-collector fan tach outputs, a low pulse at either header reverse-biases the series diode, so the MCU-side input remains pulled high instead of seeing the pulse. Fan speed/stall monitoring may therefore fail for both fans.

parsed.summary: The fan tach signal paths appear to have their series diodes reversed relative to the MCU-side pull-ups. This likely blocks the low-going pulses produced by standard open-collector fan tach outputs, undermining the specified fan monitoring.
